analysis.title: "Some Were Getting Cold Feet": Hock Tan Pays Up, Guarantees The Loss To Get Anthropic's $63 Billion Chip Deal Done
key_insights: Broadcom (AVGO) arranged a $63B financing with Bank of America, Blackstone, Citigroup and Morgan Stanley. A new SPV buys Broadcom XPU accelerators and networking gear and leases them to Anthropic, with deliveries starting in 2027.

BofA, Citi and MS arranged the first lien. Blackstone is the sole provider of the committed second lien. Broadcom provides residual value support to the SPV equal to the first lien portion, about $43.5B or 69% of the total per Reuters.

Per the WSJ, some banks got cold feet and felt they were not paid enough for the risk. Hock Tan held weekend talks with bank executives, agreed to higher interest rates and gave lenders more comfort on Broadcom's guarantees in case Anthropic defaults.

The deal grew from the Oct 2 Bloomberg report of $60B, when syndication letters were out for a $42B senior-secured tranche with Blackstone leading an $18B junior piece. The final deal is $63B with about $43.5B of first lien.

Broadcom's exposure to Anthropic totals roughly $114B: up to $29B backstop on the June Big Sky SPV (per a company filing), about $43.5B of residual value support on North Star, and a $42B convertible note facility. The facility converts into non-voting Class N shares at 90% of the 30-day VWAP (85% if Anthropic misses revenue targets). A $50B-plus OpenAI chip financing is still in the works.

Anthropic's S-1 shows about $637B of named compute commitments (roughly $780-810B including estimated TPU and AMD tranches). The largest line is about $161.2B of rent on five-year Broadcom master equipment leases for Google TPU hardware.

Anthropic disclosed $16.3B of first-half revenue and $80.7B of first-half net loss, of which $72.4B came from marking up convertible notes and other instruments. It held $131.7B of cash and short-term investments at June 30. The $63B North Star financing is almost four times first-half revenue.

First-lien lenders mostly hold Broadcom credit risk, since Broadcom covers any shortfall if the chips are worth less than the loan at lease end. Blackstone's second lien carries the actual AI lab risk.
Moody's calls Broadcom one of the strongest large technology companies but warned risk would rise if it did multiple transactions in a short period to meet frontier AI labs' funding needs.
Broadcom's 5-year CDS reached 133bp by mid-October, a few bps below its record 136bp and more than triple its May level.

Goldman's Shelofsky said the IG hyperscaler basket widened 17bps in the prior week, its worst week on record outside of July's similar moves, and the 30-year hyperscaler basket was at new wides, 85bps cheap to the IG100 ex-hyperscalers. SPCX 2031s were 55bps wider on the week.
On Monday Meta CDS closed 10bps tighter and chip names 2-3bps tighter, while SpaceX and Oracle went 5bps wider. By Tuesday morning the IG hyperscaler basket was 2.5bps off its Monday tights.
Goldman's credit dashboard shows USD CCC spreads at 1,118bp, up 298bp in three months and at the 100th percentile of the past three years, with the 10-year at 4.99%.

Meta's common stock offering was upsized to $25B at $625 per share, alongside $12.5B of mandatory converts and a $60B ATM program, for $97.5B in total, the largest equity raise ever per Reuters. Nvidia said it would put in $3B.

Monday's AI capital raising came to roughly $200B in one day, including Broadcom's $63B, Meta's equity raise and SpaceX's $40B Nvidia chip lease with Apollo. The chip-debt tally is about $278B, excluding Oracle's unsized SPV and Nvidia's $500B compute financing platform.

Goldman's Privorotsky said the cost of capital has risen materially and sustained relief in credit would be a powerful catalyst. His four hyperscaler paths: capex accelerates on expensive debt, capex cut for lack of financing, capex funded by organic cash flow, or capex flat/up with more equity financing.

JPMorgan's International Market Intelligence desk says the IPO news plus Meta and AVGO/SPCX financings make a material capex cut for lack of financing less likely, but concerns on monetization are unresolved. A JPM FICC view says circular financing and Nvidia credit support may be needed to finance depreciating GPUs through investment-grade markets, with concentration and correlated downside risks. Banks are buying CDS protection on data center lending exposure.

market_movers.rationale: The article argues risk from the AI chip financing now sits on Broadcom's balance sheet, with CDS near record wides. The stock was up 2.3% to about $336 premarket on the deal.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up 298bp in three months and at the 100th percentile of the past three years, showing stress in low-rated credit.
Per Goldman's morning credit dashboard, high yields add to the cost of financing the AI buildout.

risk_factors: Concentration of Broadcom's guarantees and lending in a single customer, about $114B, with more pending for OpenAI.
Circularity: Broadcom sells chips, lends to the customer, guarantees the lenders and buys customer stock, so risks are correlated.
Monetization concerns are cited as the cause of the financing bottleneck.
Possible Moody's action if Broadcom does multiple large transactions in a short period.
Rising cost of capital and wider hyperscaler and CCC credit spreads.
Chip resale value falling below the loan balance at lease end, which Broadcom must cover.
vol_and_positioning: Broadcom 5-year CDS at 133bp in mid-October versus a record 136bp, more than triple its May level.
IG hyperscaler basket widened 17bps in a week, with the 30-year basket 85bps cheap to the IG100 ex-hyperscalers.
Banks are buying CDS protection to hedge growing data center lending exposure, per JPM's desk.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's Molavi described vendor financing as 'balance sheet as a service'.
JPMorgan's International Market Intelligence desk sees the glass half full against Goldman's Privorotsky, who calls AI credit the most important thing to watch.

tension_points.bull_case: The money is there, Anthropic's revenue is compounding, deliveries start in 2027 and the IPO will have recapitalized the tenant. JPMorgan's desk says the Meta and AVGO/SPCX financings make a capex cut for lack of financing less likely.
tension_points.bear_case: Banks lent only after the vendor guaranteed the debt and raised the coupon, so risk sits on Broadcom's balance sheet. Circular financing creates concentration and correlated downside, and Broadcom CDS is near record wides.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Moody's warned Broadcom risk rises with multiple transactions in a short period, and Broadcom is working on the next one (OpenAI).

tension_points.bull_case: Credit caught a bid Monday as the Meta, SpaceX and Broadcom deals cleared. Goldman says sustained relief in credit would be a powerful catalyst.
tension_points.bear_case: By Tuesday the IG hyperscaler basket was 2.5bps off its Monday tights, and CCC spreads sit at the 100th percentile of three years.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Goldman's Shelofsky said a bounce could not happen until the Meta and SpaceX chip deals cleared, and both are now cleared, so renewed widening would invalidate the relief thesis.

theme_stances.key_argument: Banks needed the vendor's guarantee to lend against the vendor's own product to a customer with large losses, so the risk sits on Broadcom's balance sheet.
theme_stances.evidence: the risk in the trade sits squarely on Broadcom's balance sheet
